decisions.reason: The positive comments about the integrated form factor do not change the accepted enclosure size or bowl-well constraints.
The source does not change the required cup size, clearance, or raised height.
The upper-tower rigidity concern does not change the separate platform's type, height, purpose, or footprint.
The client specifically requires accessibility and serviceability from underneath for future maintenance, adding a location-specific access constraint not represented in the current state.

source_message.speaker: client
source_message.text:
Hey Larry, These updates are looking really good. It’s awesome seeing the machine move from individual parts into an actual integrated system. The overall form factor is starting to come together really nicely and the curved spout/tower design looks much cleaner and more product-oriented than I was imagining from the earlier renders. I also really like seeing the drainage routing and plumbing integration underneath the bowl. It’s encouraging seeing the functional side of the system being solved physically now instead of just conceptually in CAD. A few things I’m still thinking about as the build progresses: 
 splash control once the whisk is spinning at higher RPMs structural rigidity/vibration of the upper tower during operation ease of cleaning and sanitation access for anything touching liquid accessibility/serviceability underneath if maintenance is needed later But overall this is all very exciting progress and definitely feels like the machine is becoming a real product now instead of just a concept. Looking forward to seeing the upcoming videos/testing footage. 

Karla Burton

value_updates.underside_service_access: Provide accessibility and serviceability underneath the machine for future maintenance.

decisions.reason: The concern about splash control at higher RPMs is already represented by the current high-speed splash behavior and does not establish a new method or constraint.
Approval of the visible plumbing integration does not change solenoid actuation, isolation, or closed-state behavior.
The source does not discuss or change the master power control or its placement.
Upper-tower rigidity is owned by the structural-stability Requirement and does not change the candidate's electrical load-capacity or general event-use reliability state.
The source contains no decision about the raised-base logo, font, leaf, or letter case.
The general concern about sanitation access does not change the independently defined bowl-removal clearance or event swapping workflow.
Positive commentary about the curved spout design does not establish a new geometry, orientation, fabrication, or pour-direction constraint.
Mention of higher RPMs provides operating context for splash and vibration concerns but does not change the selected speed range or control behavior.
